name: IBM Quantum
description: IBM's quantum division. Builds superconducting processors, runs a public cloud fleet and develops the Qiskit software stack.

name: Google Quantum AI
description: Alphabet's quantum lab. Builds superconducting processors such as Sycamore and Willow and focuses on error correction.

name: Microsoft Quantum
description: Microsoft's quantum program. Pursues topological qubits and offers Azure Quantum, a cloud platform hosting several hardware partners.

name: Amazon Web Services (Braket)
description: Amazon's quantum efforts: the Braket cloud service for third-party hardware and the AWS Center for Quantum Computing, which builds cat-qubit chips.

name: NVIDIA
description: GPU maker whose CUDA-Q platform and cuQuantum libraries support quantum simulation and hybrid quantum-classical computing.

name: Intel
description: Develops silicon spin-qubit chips made with conventional semiconductor manufacturing, plus cryogenic control electronics.

name: Honeywell
description: Industrial conglomerate and majority owner of Quantinuum.

name: Fujitsu
description: Japanese IT company building superconducting quantum computers with RIKEN, alongside its quantum-inspired Digital Annealer.

name: IonQ
description: Trapped-ion quantum computer maker that has expanded into networking and sensing through acquisitions.

name: Quantinuum
description: Trapped-ion hardware and software company formed from Honeywell Quantum Solutions and Cambridge Quantum. Known for its H-series machines.

name: Rigetti Computing
description: Designs and fabricates superconducting quantum processors and offers them through the cloud.

name: D-Wave Quantum
description: Pioneer of quantum annealing for optimization problems, also developing gate-model superconducting systems.

name: PsiQuantum
description: Aims to build a large fault-tolerant photonic quantum computer using silicon photonics made in commercial chip fabs.

name: Xanadu
description: Photonic quantum computing company and creator of the PennyLane quantum machine learning library.

name: QuEra Computing
description: Neutral-atom quantum computer company spun out of Harvard and MIT research.

name: Pasqal
description: French neutral-atom quantum computing company.

name: Atom Computing
description: Builds large neutral-atom qubit arrays and partners with Microsoft on logical qubits.

name: Infleqtion
description: Neutral-atom company (formerly ColdQuanta) working on quantum computing, clocks and sensors.

name: planqc
description: German neutral-atom quantum computing startup from the Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics.

name: IQM Quantum Computers
description: European maker of superconducting quantum computers for research centers and companies.

name: Alice & Bob
description: Builds superconducting cat qubits designed to suppress bit-flip errors.

name: Oxford Quantum Circuits
description: UK superconducting quantum computing company using a 3D 'coaxmon' qubit design.

name: Quantum Circuits Inc
description: Yale spin-out building superconducting systems with built-in error detection (dual-rail qubits).

name: SEEQC
description: Develops digital superconducting (SFQ) chips that control and read out qubits inside the fridge.

name: Origin Quantum
description: Chinese quantum computing company building superconducting processors and a cloud platform.

name: Alpine Quantum Technologies
description: Austrian trapped-ion company from the University of Innsbruck, known for rack-mounted quantum computers.

name: Oxford Ionics
description: Trapped-ion company that controls qubits with electronics instead of lasers. Acquired by IonQ in 2025.

name: Universal Quantum
description: UK trapped-ion company designing modular chips linked by electric fields.

name: eleQtron
description: German trapped-ion company using microwaves rather than lasers to drive qubits.

name: Quantum Art
description: Israeli trapped-ion startup focused on multi-qubit gates and large-scale architectures.

name: Quandela
description: French photonic quantum computing company built around semiconductor single-photon sources.

name: ORCA Computing
description: UK photonic company building fiber-based systems with quantum memory.

name: QuiX Quantum
description: Dutch photonic company making silicon-nitride photonic processors.

name: Quantum Computing Inc
description: US company focused on thin-film lithium niobate photonics and photonic optimization machines.

name: Diraq
description: Australian silicon spin-qubit company from UNSW, aiming at CMOS-compatible chips.

name: Silicon Quantum Computing
description: Builds atom-scale qubits from phosphorus atoms placed precisely in silicon.

name: Quantum Motion
description: UK silicon spin-qubit company using standard CMOS manufacturing.

name: Equal1
description: Irish company building silicon spin-qubit servers that integrate qubits and control on chip.

name: Photonic Inc
description: Canadian company linking silicon spin qubits with photons to build networked quantum computers.

name: Nord Quantique
description: Canadian company encoding error-correctable qubits in bosonic modes (GKP states).

name: Quantum Brilliance
description: Builds room-temperature quantum accelerators using nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond.

name: Classiq
description: Quantum software platform that synthesizes optimized circuits from high-level models.

name: Q-CTRL
description: Quantum control and error-suppression software, also developing quantum navigation sensors.

name: Riverlane
description: UK company building the quantum error correction stack, including real-time decoders.

name: Phasecraft
description: Develops near-term quantum algorithms for materials and chemistry simulation.

name: Algorithmiq
description: Quantum algorithms company focused on life sciences and error mitigation.

name: QC Ware
description: Quantum and quantum-inspired software for chemistry and drug discovery.

name: Multiverse Computing
description: Quantum and quantum-inspired software, including tensor-network compression of AI models.

name: SandboxAQ
description: Alphabet spin-out combining AI and quantum techniques for simulation, sensing and post-quantum cryptography.

name: Horizon Quantum Computing
description: Singapore company building programming tools that compile classical code to quantum programs.

name: Qedma
description: Error suppression and mitigation software for running longer circuits on today's hardware.

name: Strangeworks
description: Platform giving access to many quantum and classical compute providers through one interface.

name: 1QBit
description: Canadian quantum and advanced computing software company.

name: Agnostiq
description: Makers of Covalent, an open-source workflow tool for hybrid quantum and HPC jobs.

name: Terra Quantum
description: Swiss company offering quantum algorithms, hybrid computing and security services.

name: Quantum Machines
description: Makes control hardware and software (OPX, QUA) used to run qubits across platforms.

name: Bluefors
description: Leading maker of dilution refrigerators that cool superconducting and spin qubits.

name: Oxford Instruments
description: Scientific instruments company supplying cryogenic systems and tools for quantum research.

name: Zurich Instruments
description: Makes signal generators and analyzers used for qubit control and readout.

name: Qblox
description: Dutch maker of scalable qubit control stacks, spun out of QuTech.

name: ID Quantique
description: Long-standing quantum key distribution and quantum random number company, now majority owned by IonQ.

name: Toshiba (Quantum Key Distribution)
description: Toshiba's quantum key distribution business, active in fiber QKD networks in the UK and Japan.

name: Arqit Quantum
description: UK encryption company selling quantum-safe key agreement software.

name: Qunnect
description: Builds hardware for quantum networks over existing telecom fiber.

name: Aliro Quantum
description: Software for designing, simulating and running quantum networks.

name: QuSecure
description: Post-quantum cryptography company helping organizations migrate to quantum-safe encryption.

name: PQShield
description: UK post-quantum cryptography company supplying hardware and software implementations.

name: Qnami
description: Makes scanning NV-diamond magnetometers for imaging materials at the nanoscale.
